newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ annual report acknowledges strain on exports.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ annual report acknowledges strain on exports.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash said in the bank's annual report published on Wednesday that tight monetary conditions were placing strain on exporters but easing for the sake of temporary relief would solve nothing long term and leave exporters facing higher inflation.
He said the 1995/96 year was a very challenging one for the bank, and 1996/97 looked set to follow in the same vein.
"Looking forward, 1996/97 seems likely to be no less challenging than 1995/96," Brash wrote in the bank's Annual Report. His commentary was prepared before the RBNZ's September 13 economic statement.
"We will be faced with the task of formulating monetary policy in order to get inflation firmly back towards the middle of the target band, without driving inflation below the floor of that band."
Brash said he had no doubt that underlying inflation would soon be restored to the target band.
September quarter data was surprisingly weak, taking annual underlying inflation to 2.34 percent against the bank's forecast of 2.7 percent.
Markets are awaiting the bank's next Monetary Policy Statement on December 17 to see to what extent that lower figure will alter the bank's economic expectations.

Brash said the RBNZ's new disclosure regime for supervising banks, implemented in the 1995/96 year, may need some minor fine tuning. On the whole, however, the RBNZ was very pleased with its operation.

"It is in the nature of the case, however -- with forecasting being an inherently uncertain business and monetary policy taking many months to have its full impact on inflation -- that inflation will on occasion move outside that target," he said.

In its latest economic projections in September, the RBNZ forecast December year underlying inflation at 2.5 percent, falling to 2.1 percent in the March year and back into the target band in the June year, at 1.5 percent.
The bank has battled with annual inflation on or outside the ceiling of its 0-2 percent target band for six quarters.
"We have not been quite so fortunate with the introduction of a system of real-time gross settlements in the inter-bank payments system," he said.

The RBNZ had hoped the system would be operation by mid 1996. However, the "considerable complexities" of implementing the new system meant it was unlikely to be fully operational until late 1996 or early 1997, Brash said.
